input.label: Unvetted transit candidate · absent in 6 other seasons

checks.name: Host star parameters
checks.detail: TESS Input Catalog v8.2; luminosity class dwarf

checks.name: Companion radius
checks.detail: Jupiter-sized: brown dwarfs and low-mass stars have this radius too, so only a mass (RVs) can tell

checks.name: Host type
checks.detail: a main-sequence dwarf (Teff 5582 K)

checks.name: Multiplicity
checks.detail: no sign of a companion in Gaia DR3 (astrometry, image shape, orbit and binary tables) or on ExoFOP
checks.value: Gaia DR3 RUWE 0.87, IPD harmonic 0.005, multi-peak 0% · ExoFOP companions 0

checks.name: Already catalogued
checks.detail: not a TOI, CTOI, known planet or catalogued binary at this period
checks.value: checked: TOIs, CTOIs, confirmed planets, TESS EB catalog, AAVSO VSX, Gaia DR3 eclipsing binaries and orbits

checks.name: Individual transits
checks.detail: the period is supported by 24 independent transits
checks.value: 24 transits with data in 15 sectors; 3 individually ≥ 3σ

checks.name: Engineering data
checks.detail: no transit falls in a known engineering interval

checks.name: Raw flux (SAP)
checks.detail: the dip is in the raw aperture flux too, not made by the detrending
checks.value: 24 transits: pipeline flux 0.808 ppt ± 0.213, raw SAP 0.684 ppt ± 0.214; s64 QLP, s65 QLP, s66 QLP, s67 QLP, s68 QLP, s69 QLP, s87 QLP, s88 QLP, s89 QLP, s90 QLP, s93 QLP, s94 QLP, s95 QLP, s96 QLP, s97 QLP

checks.name: Background correlation
checks.detail: the dip doesn't follow the pipeline's background estimate
checks.value: raw SAP 0.684 ppt ± 0.214; with the background regressed out 0.408 ppt ± 0.212; flux-background correlation |r| 0.24 within ±1.5 d

checks.name: Event consistency
checks.detail: 1 transit is far deeper than the rest (up to 6.7σ): a systematic or another source at those times
checks.value: χ²/dof 3.68 over 24 transits; 1 more than 4σ deep (BTJD 3193.01); without the 3 strongest: 0.912 ppt, SNR 4.0

checks.name: Signal uniqueness (model-shift)
checks.detail: the transit stands out from every other phase by more than the red noise allows
checks.value: after removing 5 pulsation signals (before: 8.1σ red, F_red 1.23): primary 10.1σ white, 8.0σ red (F_red 1.25); next dip 4.5σ, strongest brightening 5.0σ; thresholds 5.0σ / 2.6σ; MS1 3.0, MS2 1.8, MS3 1.5

checks.name: SNR growth
checks.detail: SNR grew to 5.8, half or less of the 84.5 that √N predicts: the new transits add almost nothing
checks.value: SNR 5.8 over 24 transits (found at SNR 24.4 on 2; √N predicts 84.5)

checks.name: Period consistency
checks.detail: every covered transit lines up with the ephemeris; 2P is tested by odd/even in Stage 2

checks.name: Alias periods
checks.detail: P/2 to P/5 each predict transits where the data show none

checks.name: Detrending sensitivity
checks.detail: survives 4 detrendings (two methods, transits masked) with the depth within 30%
checks.value: running median 0.5 d: 1.22 ppt (SNR 6.1); running median 1 d: 1.17 ppt (SNR 5.8); running median 2 d: 1.07 ppt (SNR 5.3); local quadratic 1.5 d: 1.18 ppt (SNR 5.9)

checks.name: Depth stability
checks.detail: depth differs: s69 30.2 ppt vs 1.17 ppt overall (6.7σ, by sector)

checks.name: Odd/even depths
checks.detail: alternate transits agree within 3σ

checks.name: Secondary eclipse
checks.detail: no secondary eclipse at phase 0.5 or elsewhere
checks.value: phase 0.5: -0.464 ppt (-2.0σ); deepest elsewhere: phase 0.38, 0.715 ppt (2.9σ); σ include red noise (×1.25)

checks.name: Transit shape
checks.detail: SNR 5.8 is too low to tell a V from a U

checks.name: Duration vs expected
checks.detail: consistent with a transit across this star
checks.value: 3.59 h measured vs 4.10 h for a central transit (ratio 0.88)

checks.name: Stellar density
checks.detail: ingress not resolved (SNR 5.8, ingress 0.09 h)

checks.name: Variability at the transit period
checks.detail: no variability above 0.5 ppt out of transit (smaller pulsations are handled by the pulsation test)
checks.value: no significant variability in 8 sectors

checks.name: Pulsation removal
checks.detail: the transit survives subtracting the star's pulsations, at the same depth
checks.value: 1 periodic signal removed: 8.97 h (1.08 ppt); transit 1.16 ppt (SNR 5.1) → 1.17 ppt (SNR 5.2), 8 sectors

checks.name: Archival radial velocities
checks.detail: no archival RVs: Gaia DR3 has no RV time series for the star (too faint or too hot for RVS); not in APOGEE DR17

checks.name: Centroid shift
checks.detail: no significant centroid motion: the source is within ~60″ of the target (3σ)
checks.value: 15 sectors; implied source offset 13.9 ± 15.4″ (shift 0.0σ)

checks.name: Difference imaging
checks.detail: ran on 4 sectors, but no source visible in the pixels (0.3σ): the transit is too shallow for TESS's full-frame images; it can't say which star dims
checks.value: s98: 4 transits, source 0.0σ; s97: 3 transits, source 0.3σ; s96: 2 transits, source 0.0σ; s95: 1 transits, source 0.0σ

checks.name: Own pixel photometry
checks.detail: our own photometry of the pixels is too noisy here to confirm or rule out the dip
checks.value: s97, s96, s95: 0.163 ppt ± 0.554 with column-wise background, 0.193 ppt ± 0.478 without; pipeline 0.864 ppt ± 0.356 at the same transits (expected here ~0.691 ppt)

checks.name: Detector position
checks.detail: well inside the CCD
checks.value: no dead row or column in the cutout

checks.name: Aperture growth
checks.detail: too noisy in our own photometry to say whether the dip keeps its depth in a bigger aperture
checks.value: s97, s96, s95: r 1 px (3 px) 0.203 ppt ± 0.739, r 3 px (28 px) 0.66 ppt ± 0.916; expected in the large one from the neighbours' dilution 0.164 ppt

checks.name: Pointing jitter
checks.detail: no extra pointing jitter during the dip

checks.name: Aperture dependence
checks.detail: large/small depth ratio 2.83 (3.2σ). Not scored: QLP's 1x1 and 5x5 px apertures aren't dilution-corrected, and known on-target planets differ by up to 3x too; a pixel-level (TPF) test is needed
checks.value: small 0.618 ppt ± 0.156, large 1.75 ppt ± 0.317 (QLP, 15 sectors)

checks.name: Nearby sources
checks.detail: 9 stars within 1′ (3 TESS pixels) could make the dip and the pixel and centroid tests rule out the other 53: needs seeing-limited photometry of the neighbours on a transit night
checks.value: 62 of 101 Gaia DR3 stars within 2′ could cause a 1.17 ppt dip if eclipsed: Gaia 5284833532606116736 at 16″, T 20.6 (needs a 95% eclipse); Gaia 5284833532607714560 at 25″, T 19.8 (needs a 45% eclipse); Gaia 5284833532606118784 at 40″, T 20.0 (needs a 54% eclipse); Gaia 5284833734468582016 at 46″, T 16.9 (needs a 3% eclipse)

checks.name: Unresolved companions
checks.detail: Gaia sees no companion beyond ~1″ (512 au at 512 pc), and RUWE 0.87 disfavours bright ones at ~0.1-1″; closer than ~0.5-1″ (256 au at 512 pc) only speckle/AO imaging can look (the statistical validation below allows for them)
checks.value: RUWE 0.87 · no Gaia source within 4″

checks.name: Ground photometry (ZTF archive)
checks.detail: 1.17 ppt is too shallow for ZTF's ~1-2% per-point precision

checks.name: Saturation
checks.detail: too faint to saturate
checks.value: Tmag 13.33

checks.name: Crowding
checks.detail: no SPOC crowding estimate or TIC contamination ratio

checks.name: Independent pipelines
checks.detail: no sector with a transit has a second pipeline's light curve

checks.name: Another season
checks.detail: seen in TESS data more than a year apart
checks.value: transits in 4 TESS years (data in 4)

checks.name: Kepler/K2 archive
checks.detail: neither Kepler nor K2 observed the star
checks.value: no KIC or EPIC id: not a Kepler / K2 target

checks.name: False-positive probability
checks.detail: a nearby false positive is plausible (an approximate TRICERATOPS-style calculation: run TRICERATOPS with a contrast curve before claiming validation)
checks.value: FPP 22%, NFPP 20%; most likely: Planet transits the target 62%, Planet transits the target, diluted by an unresolved bound companion 16%, Neighbour Gaia 5284833734468582016 is an eclipsing binary 6.5%

checks.name: High-resolution imaging
checks.detail: speckle or AO imaging to find companions at 0.05-2″ (none on ExoFOP yet)

checks.name: Ground photometry
checks.detail: deep enough for 0.4-1 m telescopes; next transits 2026-11-10 23:37 UTC, 2026-11-26 21:48 UTC, 2026-12-12 19:59 UTC (BJD-based; UTC differs by up to ~8 min)

checks.name: Reconnaissance RVs
checks.detail: a 0.08 M☉ companion at P 15.9 d would give K ≈ 6.82 km/s: a few spectra at ~100 m/s rule out a stellar companion and show double lines

checks.name: Precision RVs
checks.detail: K ≈ 81.4 m/s for ~318 M⊕ (mass from radius, Chen & Kipping 2017; giants span Saturn to brown-dwarf masses); faint for precision RVs

notes: Approximate re-implementation of TRICERATOPS (circular orbits, main-sequence companions, Sun-like hosts for background stars and for neighbours without a Gaia size); run TRICERATOPS/VESPA before claiming validation.
No high-resolution imaging: unresolved companions within ~1″ (75% of binaries at 512 pc) are allowed.
No archival RVs: the target's eclipsing-binary companions are not mass-limited.
Only the 12 most plausible of 62 viable neighbours were modelled.
Target scenarios assume the light curve is already corrected for neighbours' contaminating flux; eclipsing companions at other periods (x2P for bound/background stars) are not modelled.
